A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Stereotactic radiotherapy pathway for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated. Every stage I patient who is too frail for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy (3-8 visits, no anaesthesia) instead of being left without treatment. The treatment exists in every university hospital; what is missing in some counties is the referral rule.
effect_summary_en: In the Netherlands, 7% fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated once stereotactic radiotherapy was fully available (2007-2009 vs 2001-2003); the share of all lung cancer patients is not reported.
supported_en: The Netherlands Cancer Registry study (Annals of Oncology 2012) found a 7% absolute fall in untreated elderly stage I patients after stereotactic radiotherapy was introduced.
not_supported_en: No page gives the 0.8-point gain in the share of all patients; that figure rests on our own assumption of an 8% patient share.
in_use_quote: Jos leikkaus ole mahdollinen, hoitomuoto voi olla korkea-annoksinen niin sanottu täsmäsädehoito osassa tapauksia.
in_use_summary_en: HUS's lung cancer pathway page (updated 15.06.2026) says high-dose targeted radiotherapy may be used in some cases when surgery is not possible; South Karelia's own radiotherapy unit has two linear accelerators and a PET-CT, and its 2026 accelerator tender listed SBRT body fixation as an option.
missing_en: No page shows a rule that every inoperable stage I patient is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy.
summary_en: HUS's lung cancer pathway page says that high-dose targeted radiotherapy may be used in some cases when surgery is not possible. South Karelia runs its own radiotherapy unit with a PET-CT scanner, and in 2026 it put out a tender for an accelerator that included SBRT fixation as an option. No page shows a rule that every inoperable stage I patient is referred. A Dutch registry study (Annals of Oncology 2012) found 7% fewer untreated elderly stage I patients after SABR became available, which supports the direction of our assumed effect but not its size across all patients.
unanswered_en: I found no page from Ekhva or HUS that states a referral rule for stereotactic radiotherapy or gives how many inoperable stage I patients go untreated in the county.
